When an asser
tion is authored on an individual prompt turn it is evaluated against **that turn's slice** of the transcript — tool calls, assist
ant message, tool errors, and widget observations for that turn only. `Token budget under N` is case-only because per-turn token u

sage is not reliably captured; all other assertions are turn-scopable.

> [!NOTE]
>
--
> N` remains a valid assertion and k
eeps working wherever it is already authored,\n> but for spend, two things replace it: [cost on every run](#cost), which shows\n>
what a suite actually costs, and `--max-cost-increase-percent`, which fails CI\n> when a change makes the suite more expensive rel
ative to its own baseline. For\n> a ceiling on what the whole organization may spend, see the [spend\n> budget](https://docs.mcpja

m.com/hosted/overview.md#spend-budget).
--
>
> If **Run all** is disabled, no models are selected or a run for that suite is al
ready in progress. For non-environment suites, a missing connected server also disables it. When every model the suite would run i
s out of MCPJam credits, **Run all** and each case's **Run** button are disabled with an \"Out of MCPJam credits · resets in …\" t
ooltip — switching any case to a model from your own providers re-enables those buttons. The header pickers will tell you which co

ndition applies.

### Run review

--

### Pre-run credit estimate

When enabled on your account, an **ⓘ** icon appears bes
ide run controls before you launch. Hovering it shows an estimated credit cost for the run about to start — priced against the exa

ct models, cases, and iteration count the button will execute.

The estimate appears on:

--
| - | - |
| Estimated: \~N cre
dits — based on your recent runs | Full coverage, grounded in your own run history |\n| Estimated: \\~N credits — partly based on
recent runs | Full coverage, partially grounded in history |\n| Rough estimate: \\~N credits — improves after first run | Full cov
erage, heuristic only (no history yet) |\n| At least \\~N credits — part of this run is unpriced | Some models or run slices could

not be priced |
| Estimate unavailable for these models | No pricing data available |

1 credit = \$0.01. Your free daily all
owance and any BYOK keys change what is actually deducted. The estimate is informational only — it never blocks or gates a run.\n\

n### Frozen execution snapshots

--
* **Suite accuracy** — pass rate of the most recent run, with the last three runs' trend so
you can see whether you're improving or regressing.\n* **Run insights** — an AI-written diff against your previous completed run:
which cases moved, which tools changed behavior, which models diverged. Skim this first; it usually points at the right rabbit ho
le. The model pass is **included with MCPJam and consumes no credits**; it counts against a daily insight quota shared with swarm
wave and user-testing insights. Guests browsing without a signed-in account will see a **Sign in** prompt in the insights band — s
igning in unlocks the feature without losing your place.\n* **Overview tab** — every run with its summary metrics, plus a Suite He
alth chart whose bars link to individual run rows. Click in for the iteration-level breakdown. The table shows **Date** first, the
n **Run**, with separate **Client**, **Model**, **Platform**, **Commit**, **Rate**, **Latency**, **Tokens**, and **Calls** columns
. The Client column counts unique clients; when there are more than two, a **+N** badge appears — hover it to see all clients in a
tooltip.\n* **Cases tab** — every case with its latest verdict and a quick replay button. To delete a case, hover its row and cli
ck the trash icon; a confirmation dialog appears before the case is removed. The trash icon is hidden for CI-managed suites and re
ad-only configurations. You can also delete the open case from the case editor header using the same trash icon — it is hidden for
unsaved drafts.\n* **Executions tab** — a flat, filterable list of every individual test execution across all cases, sorted most-
recent-first. Each row shows the case name, result (passed/failed/pending/cancelled), and timestamp. Click any row to open it in t

he compare view.
--

When two or more host configurations are attached to a suite, a **By case / By host** toggle appears. **By
host** shows a matrix — one column per host, one row per case. Each cell shows pass/fail dots, pass rate, median latency, and tok

en usage. A host detached after runs were recorded stays visible, labelled **historical**.

### Cost
